problem: E20 found a real cross-domain categorical signature shared by 7 Experiences, but a shared category label is not by itself evidence of a shared development principle -- this had not yet been validated.

decision.decision_summary: Applied an exact-citation rule (not similarity) to check which of the 7 actually evidence the same principle: only 2 do (exp_phase959 -> exp_phase_e8). Rejected full-cluster promotion (5 of 7 lack evidence). Verified via 1 real, minimal execution that the validated principle is still live in real production code today. Generated 1 CANDIDATE_ONLY cross-domain principle from the validated 2-Experience lineage.

action.action_summary: Exact-citation domain-independence check + 1 minimal live-code reusability check (read materializeProjectBrainPhase964AutonomousChainRegistrationDesignV1.ts, confirmed expected text present). 0 Goal/Gap/Pattern/Policy modified.

result.note: Validates (does not create) a cross-domain principle; does not change this Goal's own real status, does not modify the Experience Layer, Pattern Registry, or E17's locked policy.

cause.root_cause_summary: E20's exact structural signature match proved category identity, not principle identity -- these are different claims requiring different evidence.

lesson: A shared categorical label across domains is a hypothesis, not a proof -- an exact-citation rule (does the later Experience literally reference the earlier one's ID) is a stronger, still-non-inferential form of evidence for "same principle" than co-occurrence in the same category, and rejecting the majority of an initially-promising cluster is the correct outcome when only a minority carries that stronger evidence.
